# 1 Enoch Chapter 69 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**69:1** And after this judgment they shall terrify them and make them tremble, because they have shown these things to those who dwell on the earth.

**69:2** And behold the names of those angels: the first of them is Samyaza, who was their leader; the second Araqiel; the third Armen; the fourth Kokabiel; the fifth Turiel; the sixth Rumiel; the seventh Danial; the eighth Nuqiel; the ninth Baraqiel; the tenth Azazel; the eleventh Armaros; the twelfth Batariel; the thirteenth Ananel; the fourteenth Turiel; the fifteenth Amsiel; the sixteenth Araqiel; the seventeenth Basasiel; the eighteenth Ananel; and their chief Samiazaz.

**69:3** These are their angels' names, and these are their leaders.

**69:4** And Gadreel: he it is who showed the children of men all the blows of death, and he led astray Eve, and showed the weapons of death to the sons of men — the shield and the coat of mail, and the sword for battle, and all the weapons of death to the children of men.

**69:5** And from his hand they have proceeded against those who dwell on the earth from that day and forevermore.

**69:6** And the second was named Penemue: he taught the children of men the bitter and the sweet, and he taught them all the secrets of their wisdom.

**69:7** And he instructed mankind in writing with ink and paper, and thereby many sinned from eternity to eternity and until this day.

**69:8** For men were not created for such a purpose, to give confirmation to their good faith with pen and ink.

**69:9** For men were created exactly like the angels, to the intent that they should continue pure and righteous, and death, which destroys everything, could not have taken hold of them; but through this their knowledge they are perishing, and through this power it is consuming me.

**69:10** And the third was named Kasdeja: this is he who showed the children of men all the wicked smitings of spirits and demons, and the smitings of the embryo in the womb that it may pass away, and the smitings of the soul — the bites of the serpent, and the smitings that befall through the noontide heat — the son of the serpent named Tabaat.

**69:11** And this is the task of Kasbeel, the chief of the oath, who showed the holy ones when he dwelt high above in glory, and its name is Biqa.

**69:12** And this angel besought Michael to show him the hidden name, that he might enunciate it in the oath, so that those might quake before that name and oath who revealed all the secret things to the children of men.

**69:13** And this is the power of this oath, for it is powerful and strong; and he placed this oath Akae in the hand of Michael.

**69:14** And these are the secrets of this oath, and they are strong through his oath: and the heaven was suspended before the world was created, and for ever.

**69:15** And through it the earth was founded upon the water, and from the secret recesses of the mountains come beautiful waters, from the creation of the world and unto eternity.

**69:16** And through that oath the sea was created, and as its foundation he set for it the sand against the time of its anger, and it dare not pass beyond it from the creation of the world unto eternity.

**69:17** And through that oath the depths are made fast and abide and stir not from their place from eternity to eternity.

**69:18** And through that oath the sun and moon complete their course, and deviate not from their ordinance from eternity to eternity.

**69:19** And through that oath the stars complete their course, and he calls them by their names, and they answer him from eternity to eternity.

**69:20** And in like manner the spirits of the water, and of the winds, and of all zephyrs, and their paths from all the quarters of the winds.

**69:21** And there are preserved the voices of the thunder and the light of the lightnings; and there are preserved the chambers of the hail and the chambers of the hoarfrost, and the chambers of the mist, and the chambers of the rain and of the dew.

**69:22** And all these believe and give thanks before the Lord of Spirits, and glorify him with all their power; and their food is in every act of thanksgiving: they thank and glorify and extol the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever.

**69:23** And this oath is mighty over them, and through it their paths are preserved and their course is not destroyed.

**69:24** And there was great joy among them, and they blessed and glorified and extolled, because the name of that Son of Man had been revealed to them.

**69:25** And he sat on the throne of his glory, and the sum of judgment was given to the Son of Man, and he caused the sinners to pass away and be destroyed from off the face of the earth, and those who have led the world astray shall be bound with chains and enclosed in their assembly-place of destruction, and all their works shall vanish from the face of the earth.

**69:26** And from henceforth there shall be nothing corruptible; for that Son of Man has appeared and has seated himself on the throne of his glory, and all evil shall pass away before his face, and the word of that Son of Man shall go forth and be strong before the Lord of Spirits.

**69:27** This is the third Parable of Enoch.

**69:28** And blessed are you, men of God, the fathers of Enoch's seed among those who remember the righteous.

**69:29** And blessed are you, men of righteousness, for you shall know the sum of all things for ever.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering from EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA. Ch. 69 is the longest and most complex chapter in the Parables. Key decisions: (1) Angel names all preserved in their Ge'ez transliteration form (all three translators agree); (2) Gadreel as corrupter of Eve (v. 4) — all three translators agree this must be preserved; (3) 'writing with ink and paper' (v. 7) as a sin — preserved without softening; (4) 'Tabaat' preserved as a proper name (v. 10); (5) 'Biqa' and 'Akae' preserved as proper names for the oath (vv. 11, 13); (6) 'that Son of Man' (vv. 24, 25, 26) — definite article preserved throughout. Divergences logged in disagreement file.*
